rows.abstract: Rationale: The softdrinks industry is well entrenched in the Philippine consumer market, amassing billions of pesos in terms of sales every year while rapidly expanding its operations. Softdrinks are regular beverages in most Filipino households, restaurants and other establishments, such that, according to studies, softdrinks have become the substitute for drinking water. It is thus an opportune time to tax softdrinks to provide a steady of funds for the development of water resources. rows.abstract: Rationale: Parking spaces are, by law, rrequired as integral provisions in the construction of business and comemrcial establishments and complexes. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING THE UTILIZATION OF RECYCLABLE RESOURCES IN CERTAIN INDUSTRIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to promote the utilization of all recyclable resources in certain specified industries. The objective of this measure is to increase the productivity of the industiries affected at the least possible cost and with a sufficient degree of utilization of recycled resources and at the same time achieving a reduction in the volume of waste.  This legislation aims to contribute to the protection and maintenance of the living environment and the healthy development of the national economy's effective utilization of resources. "Recycling Law of the Philippines" Provides for these concerns: (1) What are recyclable resources; (2) Responsibilitie s of business entities; (3) Responsibility of the government; and (4) Use of rrecyclable resources;

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY DRUG-TESTING OF DRIVERS IN PUBLIC LAND TRANSPORT COMPANIES
rows.abstract: Statistics show that in 1993 , 1.5 traffic accidents happened every hour in Metro Manila and Southern Tagalog Region alone.  4.4% of these accidents were fatal, 32% resulted in both slight and serious injuries and damage to property was estimated atP8.4B.  Thus, road safety continues  to be a serious concern of the State. Declares the following --- "SECTION 1. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, all common carriers by land, in coordination with the Land Transporatation and Franchising Regulatory Board, shall periodically conduct mandatory drug-testing on their drivers.  Such common carriers are hereby encouraged to institute a program to assist their drivers who may need rehabilitiation and after-treatment reintegration.. "

rows.abstract: Proposes these amendatory provision to RA 6506, Creating the board of Examiners for Criminologists: (1) A faculty member of any criminology school may sit in the Board; (2) Additional educational qualifiications for an applicant to the board examination include a bachelor's degree in any of the following --- (a) Police Administration; (b) Criminal Justice System Administration; (c) Security and Safety Management; (d) Convictions and Jail Management or (e) Law; and (3) Licensed criminologists with at least five (5) years of satisfactory experience in the practice of criminology CAN QUALIFY for lateral entry with the PNP as an Inspector.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO UPDATE VALUATION AND IMPROVE COLLECTION OF LAND TAXES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill therefore seeks to provide certain guidelines and policies in order to update valuation and improve collection of taxes.  The valuation takes into consideration the changes in the rate of land prices ever since the land valuation.  To implement this, the State is further ordained to establish, maintain and support an effective system of collection of land taxes. applies to lands classified as agricultural, residential, commercial, industrial, whether taxable or exempt, as deferred udner the Local Government Code. > Mandates LGUs to provide for an update on the present valuation of lands based on the fair mmarketvalue of the land to be appraised, whether agricultural, residential, commercial or industrial.

rows.title_full: AN ACT WHICH SEEKS TO INCREASE LOCAL GOVERNMENT PARTICIPATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION BY ENLARGING THE POWER OF LOCAL LEGISLATIVE BODIES IN CREATING ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL MEASURES FOR THEIR RESPECTIVE JURISDICTIONS
rows.abstract: Grants LGUs with the following powers with respect to environmental protection. (1) To approve or reject mining applications in their jurisdiction and to cancel or withdraw previously approved licenses or franchises, agreements or concessions; (2) To approve or reject applications for the oepration and maintenance o factories or plants with emissions or wastes hazardous to the environemnt; (3) To approve or reject applicaitons for forest/logging concessions or timber license agreements in theirrespective units; (4) To investigate violations committed by erring firms; (5) To impose fines, penalties and damages for violations committed by said firms; (6) To organize bodies, committees or task forces to monitor the oeprations of firms engageed in activities which have direct impact on the environment; and (7) To coordinate with people's or non-government organizations, law enforcement agencies, and other concerned agencies of the government for the enforcement of environmental laws.

rows.abstract: Declares the following --- "SECTION 1. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MAGNA CARTA OF AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT WORKERS
rows.abstract: Rationale: At present, there is a weak and fragmented agricultural service delivery operating within the Department of Agriculture and the local government units which hamper the implementation of government agricultural development programs.  One of the causes to this problem was due to the effects of devolution which made LGUs financially constrained to hire the needed agricultural development workers and provide them with the necessary compensation. Furthermore, it is unfortunate that the Local Government Code of 1991 provides that agriculturist position in the city and municipal levels be made optional, not mandatory. Besides, the position of provincial agricultural engineer, and provincial fishery officer were not even included for crreation, considering that these services are essential in accelerating agricultural modernization in the countryside. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROTECTION AND CONSERVATION OF ENDANGERED AND THREATENED SPECIES OF FISH, WILDLIFE AND PLANTS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "Philippine Endangered Species Act of 1997" Recommends the designation of particular species as either endagered or threatened based on scientific and commercial data available to the DENR Secretary. The following factors or conditions shall be considered: (1) The present or threatened destruction, modification or curtailment of its habitat or range; (2) over utilization for commercial, sporting, scientific or educational purposes; (4) inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms; and (5) othernatural or mammal factors affecting their continued existence. Penalizes violation of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 1997-06-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE PREMIUM TAX AND DOCUMENTARY STAMP TAX ON LIFE INSURANCE POLICIES AND ANNUITIES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 121 AND 183, AND AMENDING SECTION 186 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The main purpose of this bill is to lend support to a vital Philippine industry, the life insurance industry, which has been in place in our economy for almost a hundred years and among whose principal functions is the generation of domestic long term savings for economic development. Its passage will greatly support the industry's growth and development. Other countries have found such government policy economically and socially advantageous and beneficial to the country and its economy.
rows.status: Approved on Third Reading on 1997-12-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE AGE OF STATUTORY RAPE FROM TWELVE TO SIXTEEN YEARS OLD, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 335 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Seeks to AMEND Art. 335, subsection 3 of the Revised Penal Code to read as follows: "Article 335. When and how rape is committed. Rape is committed by having carnal knowledge of a woman under any of the following circumstances: (1) By using force orintimidation; (2) When the woman is deprived of reason or otherwise unconscious; and  (3) WHEN THE WOMAN IS UNDER SIXTEEN YEARS OF AGE or is demented.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1997-06-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE USE OF NON-BIODEGRADAB LE PLASTIC MATERIALS AS CONTAINERS, BAGS, WRAPPERS OR PACKAGING FOR CONSUMER PRODUCTS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: Plastic  has taken its toll against our natural environment. It accounts for a great percentage of the urban and industrial waste in the country, most of which are disposed of in rivers, esteros, seas, lakes and landfills.> Refers to inorganic materials with chemical and physical properties which prevent immediate decomposition, or materials that cannot be readily broken down by exposure to the natural environment. Penalizes the violation of this Act.
